Failed at steps 8 and 12: the message shown after changing the lead technician does not name the work order or the technician, and has no Undo button.

Tested on production, build v26.43.0-ffea43c, on 22 October 2026.

  • Set-up: Work Orders, All tab, Board View, at Truck Hill 1, in a window 1600 px wide. Search "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Reassign 9792": S1-1613 is in ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha's column and S1-1614 in ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo's column.
  • Step 8: using the keyboard as the test describes, open More actions (...) on S1-1613's card, choose Reassign lead technician, pick ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo and press Reassign. The card moves to Ben's column, but the message at the bottom right reads "Lead technician updated" with a Close button (picture 1).
  • The test expects the message "S1-1613 assigned to ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo" with an "Undo" button.
  • Step 12: open More actions (...) on S1-1614's card and choose Unassign. The card moves to Unassigned, but the message reads "Lead technician removed" with a Close button (picture 2).
  • The test expects the message "S1-1614 moved to Unassigned" with an "Undo" button.
  • Why it passed on staging on 17 October: the product has not changed, the expected message has. On 19 October the Product Owner asked for the new wording with Undo (PRD version 68, rule S4-R5, through SV-11524), and this test was updated to it that day. SV-11524 is still in Code Review, so the new message is not on production yet.

Ticket: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11524 (status Code Review, read 23 October 2026).

What needs to be done: run this test again once SV-11524 reaches production.

Failed at step 7: the mouse wheel over the empty space below a short column scrolls the whole page, so the tabs, Search, the filters and the view buttons go out of sight.

Tested on production, build v26.43.0-ffea43c, on 22 October 2026 (seen again on 23 October).

  • Set-up: browser window 1600 x 1000. Work Orders, All tab, Board View, at Truck Hill 1. Search "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Column Scroll" (Unassigned holds 25 work orders, so it is taller than the screen).
  • Before step 7, look at the top: "Create Work Order" sits on its own second line under the row of tabs and filters (picture 1).
  • Step 7: put the mouse over the empty space below a short column (for example Ayesha Khan's) and turn the wheel down. The whole page moves up 56 px: the All / Estimates / Work Orders / Completed tabs, Search, the filters and the view buttons disappear under the top bar, and the column headings move up too (picture 2).
  • The test expects the page not to move.
  • Why it fails now when it passed on staging on 19 October: the new "Technician" filter (SV-11326, Done on 20 October) was added to that row after our last staging check. With it the row is too wide for a 1600 px window, so "Create Work Order" drops to a second line, the board starts 56 px lower, and the page (1056 px) becomes taller than the window (1000 px), so it can scroll.

Report prepared and held - it is with the QA lead (story SV-10046 is Done), no ticket number yet.

What needs to be done: wait for the QA lead to decide where the report goes; run this test again after a fix.
